patch_description: The polish loop is the main quality lever, but each candidate evaluation currently recomputes all 165 triplet areas (plus full-array indexing `_min_area`). Since a candidate only moves one point, only the ~90 triplets containing that point change. Precompute, per point index, the rows of `_TRIP` containing it, maintain a full area (cross-magnitude) vector, and update only the affected entries per candidate — then take the min over the updated vector. This cuts candidate evaluation cost roughly 2×, letting us afford a richer candidate set (24 directions including the normalized gradient of the bottleneck triangle) and trying all 11 points (not just the top-3 by tight-count) within the same sub-second runtime, which increases the chance of escaping local minima and pushing min_area higher. The `while improved` loop's tight-count bookkeeping is retained but computed from the maintained area vector, so it costs nothing extra.
